text: If I make one mistake in this presentation then the whole thing will be a complete disaster.
rationale: One mistake is treated as total failure.

text: I missed one deadline so I am obviously useless at every job.
rationale: A single setback becomes a global conclusion about ability.

text: My friend has not replied yet; she must be angry with me.
rationale: The speaker assumes another person's thoughts without evidence.

text: The doctor ordered another test which means the result will definitely be terrible.
rationale: An uncertain event is interpreted as the worst possible outcome.

text: I feel incompetent today so I know I am incompetent.
rationale: A feeling is treated as proof of an objective fact.

text: I should never need help because capable people handle everything alone.
rationale: A rigid rule creates an unrealistic standard.

text: The team looked quiet after my update; I ruined everyone's mood.
rationale: The speaker takes responsibility without sufficient evidence.

text: They praised my report only because they felt sorry for me.
rationale: Positive feedback is dismissed without evidence.

text: I stumbled over one answer in class; everyone now thinks I am stupid.
rationale: The speaker assigns a negative judgment to everyone.

text: Nothing ever works out for me and it never will.
rationale: Absolute language generalizes present difficulty to all future events.

text: Either I get the highest grade or I am a failure.
rationale: Only two extreme outcomes are allowed.

text: My partner sounded tired on the phone so our relationship must be ending.
rationale: A minor ambiguous cue is escalated to relationship loss.

text: I know tomorrow's interview will go badly before I even attend it.
rationale: A negative future result is treated as certain.

text: I forgot a name at the meeting; what an idiot I am.
rationale: One behavior becomes a harsh global identity label.

text: Ten people liked the proposal but one questioned it so the proposal is worthless.
rationale: One negative response eclipses substantial positive evidence.

text: If I cannot keep everyone happy then I have failed them.
rationale: The speaker assumes responsibility for every person's feelings.

text: My manager used a short sentence in her email; I am certain I will be fired.
rationale: A neutral cue is turned into a certain severe consequence.

text: Other people cope perfectly and I am the only person who cannot manage life.
rationale: The speaker compares private struggles with an idealized view of others.

text: Because I was nervous during the call the client must have hated me.
rationale: Internal anxiety is used as evidence of another person's reaction.

text: I ate dessert after planning not to so the entire week of healthy choices is ruined.
rationale: One deviation invalidates all prior progress.

text: She cancelled dinner; people always leave me in the end.
rationale: One cancellation becomes a permanent relationship rule.

text: I must complete every task perfectly or I do not deserve to rest.
rationale: Rest is made conditional on an impossible absolute standard.

text: The bus was late on the day of my appointment because I have the worst luck in everything.
rationale: One inconvenience is generalized across the speaker's whole life.

text: My child is upset today so I must be a terrible parent.
rationale: A child's temporary emotion becomes a global parental judgment.

text: There is no point applying because they will reject me just like everyone does.
rationale: Rejection is predicted as certain and universal before acting.

text: I made an error in the report and can correct it before tomorrow's review.
rationale: The mistake is acknowledged without turning it into a global judgment.

text: My friend has not replied; she may be busy so I will check in later.
rationale: The speaker keeps multiple explanations open.

text: I am nervous about the interview but nervousness does not mean I will perform badly.
rationale: The feeling is not treated as proof of the outcome.

text: The test result is uncertain and I will wait for the doctor to explain it.
rationale: No unsupported worst-case conclusion is made.

text: One low grade is disappointing but it does not define my overall ability.
rationale: A setback is placed in proportion.

text: My manager's email was brief and I do not know why; I can ask for clarification.
rationale: The speaker avoids mind reading and seeks information.

text: I wanted the presentation to go better and I can learn from the parts that were difficult.
rationale: Imperfect performance is framed as specific and changeable.

text: Some people liked my idea and one person raised a useful concern.
rationale: Positive and negative feedback are both retained.

text: I need help with this task and asking a colleague is a reasonable option.
rationale: Needing help is not equated with incapability.

text: My partner sounded tired; I will not assume it is about me.
rationale: An ambiguous cue is not made personally meaningful.

text: I missed the train this morning but the rest of the day may still go well.
rationale: One event is not generalized to the whole day.

text: I forgot her name and felt embarrassed; people forget names sometimes.
rationale: The event is normalized without a global label.

text: I did not finish everything today though I completed the two highest-priority tasks.
rationale: Partial progress is recognized rather than classified as total failure.

text: The client declined this proposal and that does not predict how every future proposal will go.
rationale: One rejection is kept separate from future outcomes.

text: I feel sad tonight while also knowing that feelings can change.
rationale: A current emotion is accepted without making it permanent.

text: My child is upset and I can listen without deciding that I caused every feeling.
rationale: Care is expressed without excessive self-blame.

text: I would prefer a high grade but a lower grade would not make me worthless.
rationale: A preference is not converted into a rigid worth judgment.

text: The room became quiet after I spoke and there are several possible reasons.
rationale: The speaker resists assuming a single negative explanation.

text: I received criticism on one section and praise on the other sections.
rationale: Feedback is represented without filtering out positives.

text: Tomorrow could be challenging or it could go smoothly; I cannot know yet.
rationale: The future is not predicted with false certainty.

text: I chose dessert and can return to my usual meals at the next opportunity.
rationale: One choice does not erase the broader pattern.

text: I am comparing myself with her highlight reel and do not know the difficulties she faces.
rationale: The limits of the comparison are explicitly recognized.

text: I did not get the job and I am disappointed but this outcome is not my identity.
rationale: A negative result is separated from self-worth.

text: I cannot please everyone and I can still act respectfully toward them.
rationale: The speaker adopts an achievable interpersonal standard.

text: The plan failed this time so I will review what happened before deciding the next step.
rationale: The response gathers evidence instead of forming an absolute conclusion.
